title: README mentions `npm start` but there is no start script
body: The README says you can start the API with `npm start`, but package.json has no `start` script so the command fails with "Missing script: start". Add a start script that runs the server (src/server.js).

title: divide(n, 0) returns Infinity — should throw RangeError
body: `divide(10, 0)` in src/math.js silently returns `Infinity`. It should throw a `RangeError` when the divisor is zero. There is already a failing test for this in test/math.test.js.

acceptance.code:
import { test } from 'node:test'
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { divide } from '../src/math.js'
test('divide', () => {
  assert.throws(() => divide(1, 0), RangeError)
  assert.throws(() => divide(-5, 0), RangeError)
  assert.equal(divide(9, 3), 3)
  assert.equal(divide(0, 5), 0)
})

title: slugify produces repeated and leading/trailing dashes, and drops accented letters
body:
`slugify` in src/format.js has a few problems:

- `slugify('  C++ -- The   Good Parts!  ')` returns `c----the-good-parts` — repeated dashes should collapse to one: `c-the-good-parts`.
- `slugify('-Hello-')` should not start or end with a dash: `hello`.
- Accented letters are removed instead of transliterated: `slugify('Café Society')` gives `caf-society`, expected `cafe-society`.

Please fix it and add tests for these cases.

acceptance.code:
import { test } from 'node:test'
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { slugify } from '../src/format.js'
test('slugify', () => {
  assert.equal(slugify('  C++ -- The   Good Parts!  '), 'c-the-good-parts')
  assert.equal(slugify('-Hello-'), 'hello')
  assert.equal(slugify('Café Society'), 'cafe-society')
  assert.equal(slugify('The Pragmatic Programmer'), 'the-pragmatic-programmer')
  assert.equal(slugify('Déjà Vu 2'), 'deja-vu-2')
})

title: Inventory.remove lets stock go negative
body: `Inventory.remove(id, quantity)` happily drives stock below zero (e.g. removing 5 when 2 are in stock leaves -3). It should throw a `RangeError` when the quantity is not a positive integer or exceeds the current stock, and it must leave the stock unchanged in that case.

acceptance.code:
import { test } from 'node:test'
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { Inventory } from '../src/inventory.js'
test('remove guards', () => {
  const inv = new Inventory([{ id: 'a', title: 'A', author: 'X', priceCents: 100, stock: 2 }])
  assert.throws(() => inv.remove('a', 5), RangeError)
  assert.equal(inv.find('a').stock, 2)
  assert.throws(() => inv.remove('a', 0), RangeError)
  assert.throws(() => inv.remove('a', 1.5), RangeError)
  inv.remove('a', 2)
  assert.equal(inv.find('a').stock, 0)
  assert.throws(() => inv.remove('zzz', 1))
})

title: Fixed discount codes are applied after tax instead of before
body: The docs for `Cart.total()` say the discount is taken off the subtotal and tax is charged on the discounted amount, but the code taxes first and subtracts the discount afterwards. For SAVE5 (a fixed $5.00 off) on a $100.00 subtotal we currently charge $103.00; it should be ($100 - $5) * 1.08 = $102.60. Percent codes must keep working, and the total can never go below zero.

acceptance.code:
import { test } from 'node:test'
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { Inventory } from '../src/inventory.js'
import { Cart } from '../src/cart.js'
const inv = (p = 10000) => new Inventory([{ id: 'a', title: 'A', author: 'X', priceCents: p, stock: 9 }])
test('discount before tax', () => {
  assert.equal(new Cart(inv()).addItem('a').applyDiscount('SAVE5').total(), 10260)
  assert.equal(new Cart(inv()).addItem('a').applyDiscount('WELCOME10').total(), 9720)
  assert.equal(new Cart(inv(300)).addItem('a').applyDiscount('SAVE5').total(), 0)
  assert.equal(new Cart(inv()).addItem('a', 2).total(), 21600)
})

title: Support filtering GET /books by author and tag
body:
Clients need to filter the catalogue:

- `GET /books?author=martin` → books whose author contains the text (case-insensitive)
- `GET /books?tag=craft` → books that have exactly that tag
- both filters can be combined; with no filters the full list is returned as today.

Please add tests.

title: POST /cart/quote returns 500 for bad input
body:
Sending bad input to `POST /cart/quote` crashes with a 500:

- missing or empty `items`
- an item with an unknown book id
- a quantity that is not a positive integer
- an invalid `discountCode`

These are client errors and should return **400** with a JSON body `{ "error": "<helpful message>" }`. Valid requests must keep working.

title: Add a low-stock section to inventory reports
body:
Buyers want to see what is about to run out. In src/report.js:

- `summary()` should include `lowStock`: titles with 1–3 units in stock (not zero — those are already in `outOfStock`), as `{ id, title, stock }`, sorted by stock ascending then title.
- The text report and the Markdown report should both show a "Low stock" section listing them with their stock count (omit the section when the list is empty).

Don't change the other sections.

title: Rate-limit the auth middleware
body: The auth middleware in `src/middleware/auth.js` lets a client hammer `POST /login` without limits. Add rate limiting there (max 5 login attempts per minute per API key) using the existing `RateLimiter` class from `src/lib/rateLimiter.js`.

title: Paginate GET /books
body:
`GET /books` returns everything. Add pagination with `?page=` (1-based, default 1) and `?limit=` (default 20, max 50):

- the response body stays a JSON array (existing clients rely on that)
- add an `X-Total-Count` header with the total number of matching books
- invalid values (page < 1, limit < 1, non-numbers) return 400 with `{ error }`; a limit above 50 is clamped to 50
- a page past the end returns an empty array

The handler contract already supports returning `headers`.

title: Expose inventory reports over HTTP
body:
Add `GET /reports/inventory?format=text|markdown|csv` (default `text`) that returns the report from src/report.js **as plain text, not JSON**, with the right Content-Type (`text/plain; charset=utf-8`, `text/markdown; charset=utf-8`, `text/csv; charset=utf-8`). Unknown formats return 400 JSON `{ error }`.

Right now `startServer` always JSON-encodes handler bodies, so it needs to support raw string bodies too (keep JSON responses unchanged).
